thread.title: Samsung Launches Same-Day Repair Service for Galaxy Phones in U.S.

author: thestreet.com
title: Samsung Launches Same-Day Repair Service for Galaxy Phones in U.S.
text:
Samsung ( SSNLF ) just made it a lot easier for Galaxy smartphone owners in the U.S. to get their devices fixed.
The electronics giant has partnered with repair firm uBreakiFix to offer same-day, in person repairs at more than 300 locations across the country, and said that most repairs could be done within two hours. Samsung said it plans to expand the program to more than 200 additional locations by early next year.
"We live in a customer era right now where the customer experience is as important as the product," said Michael Lawder, SVP of Customer Care at Samsung Electronics America. "Our customers are busy, so want to make it as simple and effortless as we can for them to get service."
The locations will be able to replace and repair front and back screens, batteries, ports and cameras for the Galaxy S6/S6+ and later, as well as the Galaxy Note8 and Note5. There will be no charge to fix Samsung devices that are under warranty, but there will be a fee for dropped or cracked screens unless a customer subscribes to Samsung Premium Care, which costs $11.99 a month.
When asked about how Samsung's new service compares to what Action Alerts Plus holding Apple ( AAPL ) iPhone users can get at an Apple Store, Lawder said that "our focus is on delivering the best possible experience to Samsung customers; we're not really thinking about anything else."
Lawder said that Samsung plans to eventually look at providing similar service options across its vast array of consumer and home electronic devices. "With one plan, you could cover your entire Samsung experience," Lawder said. There is no timeline for expanding these services beyond Samsung's smartphones yet, however.
Samsung declined to comment on how much it is spending to launch the new service.
